To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the loss of afferent input to striatal neurons induces the formation of new synaptic contacts and dendrites.

Neuronal deafferentation in the striatum of the adult rat leads to an increase in the number and size of dendritic spines on the dendrites of surviving medium spiny neurons, and to an increase in glial fibrillary acidic protein immunoreactive astrocytes, which are associated with the deafferentation-induced changes in dendritic morphology.

the molecular correlates of synaptic reorganization in the adult central nervous system include the induction of genes that encode for growth-associated proteins and that the morphological correlates are the sprouting and reinnervation of denervated tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the cellular mechanisms underlying synaptic remodelling, with particular emphasis on the role of genomic expression in the adult brain.
the molecular, cellular, and morphological events which occur following a deafferenting lesion in the adult brain.
identifying the molecular and morphological correlates that accompany the formation of new neuronal connections following deafferentation.

the molecular mechanisms of synaptic remodeling in the adult CNS are still unknown.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the loss of synaptic connections in the aging brain is associated with a reduction in the number of synapses, an alteration in the pattern of synaptic connections and a decrease in the ability to form new synapses.
deafferentation leads to a reorganization of neuronal circuits in the central nervous systems.

the genomic response to neuronal deafferentations is not uniform and is dependent upon the cell type, the nature and severity of the deafferentation injury, and the age of the animal at the time of lesion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have a model system in which we can look at the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the process of synaptic reorganization.
the brain is capable of remodelling its synaptic circuitry, and the process of remodelling is a dynamic one.
there are a variety of ways that the brain can compensate for the loss of neurons.
